prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the elevated concrete ledge at the bottom foreground (0.5 to 1.5 m away), an upright gas cylinder with regulator and hoses within the camera wearer's arm's reach (0.5 to 1 m away in the lower right of frames 1-3, shifting to a horizontal cylinder on the lower left in frames 4-5), a sloped metal walkway extending away to the left (1.5 to 5 m), large rusted metal hoppers behind the walkway (3 to 5 m), and a recessed ground floor with stairs and machinery 4 to 8 m below and ahead in frames 4-5. In frames 1-3, a worker in an orange vest stands on the lower end of the walkway roughly 2 to 2.5 m in front of and slightly left of the camera wearer (about 1.5 m behind the foreground gas cylinder), facing and looking toward the camera wearer while within arm's reach of the walkway railings, before the camera turns left and tilts down in frames 4-5 where another worker's feet, left arm, and cylinder at the bottom-left edge (0.5 to 1 m away) and the wearer's own right hand (frame 5, 0.4 m away) enter view. Across frames 1-3 the standing worker steps slightly back and turns his torso slightly rightward while the foreground cylinder partially occludes the ledge corner, and in frames 4-5 the camera pans left and downward so the standing worker moves completely out of view to the right while the lower-left worker's body remains mostly cropped out of the frame. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map makes the vertical drop-off between the sharp foreground concrete edge and the dark recessed lower level in frames 4-5 immediately distinct from the cluttered industrial background, and clearly separates the foreground gas cylinder and hoses from the similarly coloured concrete and dirt behind them. However, the depth map is unreliable in the distant background dirt mounds and upper structures where everything saturates to uniform black beyond 5 to 6 m, and it merges the standing worker's legs and feet smoothly into the walkway surface and railing bars in frames 1-3.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates the standing worker (`person`, pink mask) on the walkway about 2 to 2.5 m ahead and slightly left of the camera wearer in frames 1-3, and captures the close-range forearms, hands, and feet of the worker on the left (`person`, 0.5 to 1 m away) alongside the camera wearer's own right hand (0.4 m away) at the bottom of frames 4-5. In frames 1-3, the standing worker faces toward the camera wearer with his head partly cropped at the top edge of frame 1 and his lower legs slightly occluded by the walkway railing, while in frames 4-5 the camera turns left and downward to show the second worker's outstretched left arm reaching within arm's reach of the wearer's right hand over the concrete ledge as they pass a wrench at 0.4 to 0.6 m distance. While the segmentation silhouette tracks the standing worker's slight retreat from frame 1 to frame 3 and clearly delineates the overlapping hands and limbs in the lower-left corner of frames 4-5 against the similarly toned concrete and cylinder in RGB, it completely omits the gas cylinders, hoses, wrench, walkways, and ledges. Furthermore, the map is highly unreliable for scene context and object identity: it hallucinates a large `elephant` mask (pink) over the rusted metal hopper behind the worker about 3 to 5 m away in frame 2 and a `surfboard` mask (brown) over a blue corrugated metal sheet lying on the ground about 4 to 5 m to the right in frame 3. It also merges the adjacent worker's left arm, legs, and the horizontal gas cylinder into a single contiguous `person` mask in frame 4, and fuses both the other worker's left arm and the camera wearer's right hand into one `person` mask in frame 5 while detaching a circular patch of the cylinder valve as a separate person fragment.
descriptions.pose: The pose map extracts 2D body keypoints (yellow) for the standing worker 2 to 2.5 m in front of the camera wearer in frames 2 and 3, and 2D hand skeletons (magenta) at the bottom foreground (0.4 to 0.8 m away) in frames 4 and 5 as the camera turns left and tilts downward. In frames 2 and 3, the shoulder, hip, and facial keypoints show the worker standing upright on the walkway facing and looking toward the camera wearer, with his left arm raised to chest height within arm's reach of the railing and shifting slightly higher from frame 2 to frame 3. In frames 4 and 5, the magenta hand skeletons pinpoint the adjacent worker's outstretched left hand entering from the lower left (about 0.6 m away, palm up) and, in frame 5, moving into contact with the camera wearer's right hand reaching in from the lower right (about 0.4 m away) to hold a wrench over the concrete ledge. The pose map makes the exact articulation of the worker's raised left arm against his high-visibility vest in frames 2-3 and the fine finger joint positions during the close-range hand interaction in frames 4-5 easier to read than in the RGB strip alone. However, the map is unreliable and incomplete across the sequence: it completely misses the standing worker in frame 1 (where the top of his head is near the frame border), fails to detect his lower left leg in frame 3 where the railing and cylinder sit nearby, omits all hand keypoints for the standing worker in frames 1-3, fails to detect the body and legs of the close-range worker partly visible at the left edge of frames 4-5, and merges the two interacting hands into a single overlapping magenta cluster in frame 5.
